desc:
The array nums is sorted in non-decreasing order and may contain duplicates. For a query value x, find two indices:

  • floor: the largest index i with nums[i] ≤ x, or -1 if no element is that small;
  • ceiling: the smallest index j with nums[j] ≥ x, or -1 if no element is that large.

Return [floor, ceiling]. If x occurs in the array, the two indices are the last and the first position of x.
constraints: nums is sorted in non-decreasing order
hints: A linear scan answers the query. The sorted order lets you discard half of the array with each comparison.
Both answers are boundaries. The ceiling index is the first position where nums[j] ≥ x; the floor index is one step before the first position where nums[i] > x.

Write one routine that returns the first index whose value satisfies a monotone test (false...false true...true). Call it with the test v ≥ x for the ceiling and with v > x for the floor (then subtract one). Map 'index equals n' to -1 for the ceiling and 'index equals 0' to -1 for the floor.
editorial: Both indices sit next to a boundary in the sorted array. Let lo be the first index with nums[lo] ≥ x (the lower bound, or n if every element is smaller) and hi the first index with nums[hi] > x (the upper bound, or n). The ceiling is lo when lo < n, otherwise -1. The floor is hi - 1, which is -1 exactly when hi = 0.

Each bound is found with a half-open binary search on [0, n): keep lo as the left end and hi as the right end, test the middle element, and move lo past it when the test is still false, otherwise set hi to it. This returns the first index where the predicate turns true. The total cost is two O(log n) searches.
